name: MI-05
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strongly Republican district (R+13 partisan lean) with incumbent Tim Walberg seeking re-election
Overwhelming fundraising gap: Walberg has $994K on hand to challenger's $13K
Prediction markets price Walberg near 92% to win
No public polling or expert ratings available, limiting precision
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Walberg: a Republican-leaning district, a well-funded incumbent, and a Democratic challenger who has raised under $56,000. Markets agree, pricing the Republican around 92%, so the race sits at the Safe R boundary with modest residual uncertainty from the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late surge of outside spending against Walberg or a major polling error in Michigan's generic ballot environment would be the main signals to monitor.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tim Walberg, the Republican incumbent, is seeking another term in a southern Michigan district that leans about thirteen points Republican. His Democratic challenger, Christian Vukasovich, has raised roughly $56,000 and holds about $13,000 on hand, while Walberg has raised $1.7 million and retains nearly $1 million for the general election. Minor-party and independent candidates are on the ballot but show no measurable support or funding.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which give the Democrat only a small chance. The forecast expects Walberg to win by roughly sixteen points, with the seat firmly in Republican hands absent an unexpected shift in the national environment.
